solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Family fortune split by the Spanish in private

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group

indicators.note: split by says the fortune word is broken open with the other piece set inside it

parts.note: your destiny is your fortune or fate
el is the Spanish word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A family inheritance divided up among Spaniards behind closed doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortune' suggests money but here means fate; 'split by' signals that the Spanish article is set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something clandestinely means doing it secretly, out of public view.

clue.text: Rejected roughly by second posh person

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly or approximately
a toff is British slang for an upper-class person

explanation.surface: Someone snubbed, more or less, by a snob for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: TOFF is British slang for a posh, upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cast-off has been discarded as no longer wanted, so it is rejected.

clue.text: Suddenly lofty about working in a church

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece and the working piece sit inside the other two pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: about says the word for lofty is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: lofty means tall, high up
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A tall person becomes busy inside a church without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TALL into LLAT; LLAT plus ON goes 'in' A + CE, giving A-LLATON-CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening all at once happens abruptly, without any build-up or warning.

clue.text: Coast of Germany with fissure

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
a rift is a crack or fissure

explanation.surface: A German coastline marked by a deep crack in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coast' looks like a noun for the shoreline but is the verb: to move along without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to move along without power or effort, just as you drift on a current.

clue.text: Decline a large settlement showing wisdom

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline
a city is a large town or settlement

explanation.surface: A big town in decline proves it has learned something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagacity is shrewd good judgement, which is another word for wisdom.

clue.text: Loom I repair to keep close to warp

indicators.note: to keep says the repair word holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: to mend is to repair

indicators.note: close to says only the final letter of warp is used

explanation.surface: A weaver fixes their loom while keeping the warp threads tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loom' looks like the weaving frame, as 'warp' suggests, but is the verb: to threaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that looms threatens to happen soon, which is what impending events do.

clue.text: Neglecting opponents on revolutionary side

parts.note: East and South are opposing partnerships at the bridge table, giving E and S
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
a wing is a side of a building or of a team

explanation.surface: A team ignores its rivals while lining up a radical on the flank.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and South sit at different sides of the table, so they are opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschewing something means deliberately avoiding or shunning it, a form of neglecting it.

clue.text: Drunk guy on green

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An intoxicated man sprawled on the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the grassy patch the drunk is lying on, but means inexperienced.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or naive, as the young often are.

clue.text: Brought to standstill and robbed

definitions.meaning: a bank ... is robbed at gunpoint

explanation.surface: Stopped in one's tracks and relieved of one's valuables.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb covers both delaying something and staging an armed robbery.

clue.text: Measure to block rat betraying

indicators.note: to block says the measure is put inside the other word, blocking it

parts.note: to sing, like to rat, is slang for informing on someone
an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Instructions for stopping vermin, with a hint of treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rat' looks like the animal but is the verb: to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Selling someone out means betraying them for gain.

clue.text: View race once beside river

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of Scotland
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Watching a historic horse race from the riverbank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is a people, not a contest; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is an image or scene, and a view is a scene one sees.

clue.text: Group of over 100 characters regularly seen in street

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: characters regularly seen in says every other letter of street is taken

explanation.surface: A crowd of more than a hundred people seen often in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth and sixth letters of 'street' give TET.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a set of eight, especially a group of musicians.

clue.text: United changed ways, getting good for time

indicators.note: getting says a new letter is taken on in the changed-ways word
for says that new letter stands in place of the one for time

parts.note: someone converted has changed their ways or beliefs

explanation.surface: A football club reformed itself and improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a team name; T (time) in CONVERTED becomes G (good).
explanation.definitionFit: Things that converged came together and met, so they were united.

clue.text: Insects on indulgent sweets

indicators.note: on in an across clue says the insects come after the indulgent word

parts.note: a fond parent is an indulgent one
ants are insects

explanation.surface: Insects crawling over a doting person's sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after, so the insects come second even though the clue names them first.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondants are soft sugary confections, a kind of sweet.

clue.text: Medical preparation tisane mixed with alcohol

indicators.note: mixed says the letters of tisane are stirred into a new order

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic spirit

explanation.surface: A remedy of herbal tea spiked with spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' turns TISANE into ANTISE.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiserum is a serum containing antibodies, given as a medical treatment.

clue.text: Playing piece from rubbish opera

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the words that follow, hidden inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slating of a terrible opera performance.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read 'piece from' as the indicator, but the definition is 'Playing piece', a chess man; 'from' alone signals the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the pieces used in a game of chess.

clue.text: House pet's noise leads to neighbour Elsie ringing landlord, maybe

parts.note: a cat's noise is a meow

indicators.note: leads to says the first letters of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: A cat's racket sets a neighbour calling the landlord about the noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ringing' looks like the phoning; with neighbour and Elsie it only gives its first letter: N, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord who owns the property they let is one example of a homeowner, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Grabbing learner in college, criminal attacked

indicators.note: grabbing says the criminal holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: a felon is a criminal
L is the learner driver's plate
up means in residence at university

explanation.surface: A villain seizes a student and assaults them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' for being at university is a British idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: To fall upon someone is to set on them suddenly, that is, to attack.

clue.text: Discussed grids, notable ones

indicators.note: discussed says the word is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound

parts.note: grates are metal grids in a fireplace

explanation.surface: Talking over crossword grids and their celebrated setters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discussed' signals a sound-alike: GRATES is said like GREATS.
explanation.definitionFit: The greats in any field are its outstanding, celebrated figures.

clue.text: Loud laugh from a wife after nonsense

indicators.note: after says the article and wife come later than the nonsense

parts.note: guff is informal for nonsense

explanation.surface: A wife bursts out laughing after hearing nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A guffaw is a hearty, boisterous burst of laughter.

clue.text: Bar got me juiced fruit

indicators.note: juiced suggests being squeezed and mashed into a new form

explanation.surface: A juice bar pressed some fruit for me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juiced' makes BAR GOT ME into a new arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The bergamot is a citrus fruit whose rind flavours Earl Grey tea.

clue.text: Explosive noise from south overwhelming old soldier

indicators.note: overwhelming says the reversed word swallows the other piece
from south in a down clue says the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a report is the bang of a gun or explosion

explanation.surface: A bang from the south swamps an elderly veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from south' reads REPORT upwards as TROPER; 'overwhelming' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trooper is a private soldier, especially in a cavalry or armoured unit.

clue.text: Rub over aluminium and wood

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the rubbing word sits above the metal

parts.note: to sand is to rub down with abrasive
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Sanding down metal and timber in the workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: SANDAL is short for sandalwood, an aromatic timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandal, or sandalwood, is a fragrant tropical tree and its wood.

clue.text: Prevent everyone going on area of many plants

indicators.note: going on says the everyone word is attached after the other

parts.note: a forest is an area thick with trees and plants
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Stopping the whole public from entering a wooded area.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall something is to act first so that it cannot happen.

clue.text: Sneak taking contents of best prizes

indicators.note: taking says the sneak word takes on the other letters

parts.note: a rat is a sneak or informer

indicators.note: contents of says the middle letters of best are used

explanation.surface: An informer pockets the pick of the awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prizes' looks like a noun but is the verb: values highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something highly is to value or esteem it, which is what prizing it means.

clue.text: Sport on moon oddly lacking publicity

indicators.note: oddly lacking says the odd-placed letters are dropped and the even ones kept

explanation.surface: No publicity for a sporting event on the moon.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'Sport on moon' leaves P, R, O, M, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A promo is a promotional item or campaign, a piece of publicity.

clue.text: Last of rolls put in good container for bread

indicators.note: put in says that letter goes inside the good word

parts.note: pure means good, morally clean

indicators.note: last of says only the final letter of rolls is used

explanation.surface: A good bag for carrying bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, so the container is a purse, not a bread bin.
explanation.definitionFit: A purse holds money, and bread is old slang for cash.

clue.text: Turned out broadcast is about racing event

indicators.note: is about says the broadcast word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a programme aired was broadcast
the TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorcycle race

explanation.surface: A race was shown on television, and people came out for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' means dressed, as in 'well turned out'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well turned out is smartly dressed, that is, attired.

clue.text: Cut, cut, cut root

indicators.note: the second cut says the first cut word itself loses its last letter

parts.note: to pare is to cut or trim
to snip is to cut

explanation.surface: A chef chops the same vegetable over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: PARE (cut) is itself 'cut', losing its E to give PAR; SNIP is the third cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A parsnip is a pale root vegetable.

clue.text: Faulty program lines run making statistical mistake

indicators.note: faulty suggests the letters are wrongly put together

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A buggy computer program produces a statistical blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faulty' rearranges PROGRAM LINES into SAMPLINGERRO; R (run) is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sampling error is the gap between a sample's figure and the true population value.
